open_points.subject: OwnerAuditAction subject-kind mapping
open_points.text:
A row of the owner audit table: which audit action (M09, R0-58) an accepted
owner action writes — for a customer mark, by its transition; for a project's
erasure, by its kind (owner, 2026-11-24) — and the form of that entry's
subject (M15–M19; owner, 2026-11-26).
open_points.question: For every owner action, customer-mark transition and project-erasure kind represented by OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS, which audit subject kind must the row contain?
options: Map each action or qualified transition/erasure kind explicitly to one of project, customer, session_project, import or none
Derive the subject kind from the audit action
Let each implementation choose the applicable subject form
open_points.default_guess: Declare an explicit mapping row for every accepted owner action that writes an audit entry.

witness.initial: Agent session S is registered and project P exists.
events: The owner grants project P to session S.
Registry writes the significant-change audit entry required for the grant.
outcomes: The OwnerAuditAction row selects subject kind project, so the entry identifies P as an ordinary project subject.
The OwnerAuditAction row selects subject kind session_project, so the entry identifies the S–P grant as a session-project subject.
witness.observer: The owner reading the audit log sees different subject facts.

open_points.subject: Audit subject kind and M15–M19
open_points.text:
Audit subject kind: `project`, `customer`, `session_project`, `import`,
  `none` — the form of an audit entry's subject, one for each of its forms
  M15–M19 (M09, M28; owner, 2026-11-26).
open_points.question: Which exact M15–M19 subject model corresponds to each of the five audit subject-kind members, and must an entry's member always match the subject model it carries?
options: The listed members correspond respectively to M15, M16, M17, M18 and M19, with matching enforced
Declare a different explicit member-to-model correspondence
The member is descriptive metadata and need not agree with the carried subject model
open_points.default_guess: Use the listed order as a respective one-to-one mapping and require the member to match the carried subject model.

open_points.subject: Audit subject kind none
open_points.text:
Audit subject kind: `project`, `customer`, `session_project`, `import`,
  `none` — the form of an audit entry's subject, one for each of its forms
  M15–M19 (M09, M28; owner, 2026-11-26).
open_points.question: What fact does subject kind `none` represent: an audit entry with no subject value, a distinct no-subject value/model, or an absent/unknown subject?
options: The entry deliberately has no subject and carries no subject value
The entry carries a distinct M15–M19 no-subject value
The subject is unknown or unavailable
open_points.default_guess: Treat none as a deliberate absence of a subject and require no subject payload.

open_points.subject: Audit subject kind model
open_points.text:
These are closed sets the specification declares; in State 6 they become
`kind: enum` or `kind: vocabulary` models without identity (SPEC_STANDARD §5).
open_points.question: Must Audit subject kind become a kind: enum runtime type or a kind: vocabulary read-only specification table?
open_points.default_guess: kind: enum, because the passage gives a closed scalar list of members.

open_points.subject: Model M28 — OwnerAuditAction
open_points.text:
Facts: the owner action; the customer mark's transition, where the action has
one; the project erasure's kind, where the action has one; the audit action it
writes; the kind of its entry's subject.
open_points.question: Replace the untyped facts list with declarations that give every OwnerAuditAction field its type, including the optionality of the transition and erasure-kind fields and the type of the audit subject kind.
